name: Milky Way
distance_note: Observation vantage point is inside the galaxy; coordinates shown are those of the Galactic Centre (Sagittarius A*).
characteristics: Our home galaxy: a barred spiral containing hundreds of billions of stars. The Sun lies about 26,700 light-years from the Galactic Centre.
discovery: Known since antiquity as a band of light; nature established in the 20th century
source: NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database (NED), compiled from published values

name: Andromeda Galaxy
distance_note: Approximate; published distances range around 2.5 Mly
characteristics: Nearest large galaxy and the most distant object visible to the naked eye. Approaching the Milky Way. Described by al-Sufi in 964 CE.
source: NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database (NED), compiled from published values

name: Triangulum Galaxy
characteristics: Third-largest galaxy of the Local Group, a gas-rich spiral with active star formation.
source: NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database (NED), compiled from published values

name: Messier 87
characteristics: Supergiant elliptical galaxy at the heart of the Virgo Cluster; hosts the black hole M87* and a prominent jet. Known for a very large globular-cluster population.
source: NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database (NED), compiled from published values

name: Sombrero Galaxy
distance_note: Approximate; published values range roughly 28–31 Mly
characteristics: Distinctive dust lane and a large central bulge, seen nearly edge-on.
source: NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database (NED), compiled from published values
